debugging_and_optimization_detail.problem_statement: The initial weight-training implementation used MSE for both activations and printed only final loss/accuracy. The user requested debugging and full optimization.
diagnosis: Sigmoid should normally use binary cross-entropy for binary classification rather than MSE.
Sigmoid cross-entropy should use predictions safely clipped away from 0 and 1 to avoid logarithm-domain numerical errors.
ReLU does not emit a probability; therefore its MSE output and threshold behavior require separate interpretation.
Initial and final loss values were needed to demonstrate that training was converging.
Input and label shape/type validation prevented silent mathematical errors.
The synthetic dataset and both activation runs needed reproducible random seeds.

implemented_changes.sigmoid_gradient: (p-y)/n, because sigmoid output combined with cross-entropy simplifies to prediction minus label.
implemented_changes.probability_clipping: Sigmoid predictions were clipped to epsilon and 1-epsilon in the loss calculation.
implemented_changes.weighted_sum_clipping: Weighted sums were clipped to [-500, 500] before sigmoid exponentiation.
implemented_changes.convergence_reporting: The loss history now exposes initial and final loss values.
implemented_changes.reproducibility: NumPy default_rng is used for the synthetic dataset and weight initialization.
implemented_changes.separate_activation_runs: The example trains and evaluates sigmoid and ReLU independently on the same dataset.

test_results_from_conversation.comparison_conclusion: Sigmoid classified every synthetic sample and had lower loss in the reported run. ReLU classified 95% and had a higher loss with the fixed setup.
